lottery_winner (07-30) traced the root cause behind the recurring 'figure buried behind the caption card' defect family ([[centered-landmark-figure-collision]] etc. are a different failure; this is the CAPTION_SAFE_ZONE note's actual mechanism): director.tsx's CountUp card is `display: inline-block`, auto-sized to whichever is WIDER, the big number (fs84 for any settled label >12 chars, e.g. any 9-figure dollar amount, else fs128) or the gold `sub` line (fs27, letterSpacing 5, roughly ~20-22px/char). The documented '~700px wide' card size in AUTOPILOT_PROMPT is only true for SHORT subs -- a verbose sub-caption (this episode's early drafts ran 50-58 chars) widens the card past 1250-1350px, burying figures that were already positioned at or past CAPTION_SAFE_X=760 by the writer. Confirmed via mid-scene stills: `boardroomNotes` (fig x=960) had its signing figure's torso fully hidden behind a 56-char sub; `fileWall` (fig x=420, scenes.tsx S02) was PARTICULARLY bad -- even with a SHORT sub, the big dollar number alone (~700-780px wide at fs84) already covers fileWall's entire figure, meaning fileWall is structurally incompatible with any dollar overlay at its default figure position, which is likely why prior episodes only ever paired fileWall with overlay=None. FIXED THIS RUN (writer-scope workaround, not a real fix): shortened all subs to ~20-30 chars, moved the new `trailerPorch` figure from x=900 to x=1220, and swapped both `fileWall` overlay-scenes to `deskSilhouette` (fig x=1180, confirmed safe) / `window` (fig x=960 but y=770, high enough to clear). CHEAP REAL FIX for a future engineering pass: cap CountUp's max-width and wrap/shrink the sub-caption font instead of letting the card grow unbounded, OR expose a per-scene safe-figure-x table keyed by template so writers/gate.py can check overlay length against it before render. Until then: writers should keep overlay `sub` under ~30 chars and avoid `fileWall`/`deskClose` (S05, fig x=400) for any scene carrying a big-number overlay.

samurai (07-13) exposed a gap between the AUTOPILOT_PROMPT/BIBLE model and duck_music's actual behavior. The prompt tells the writer: 'on the scene IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the reversal line, set gap=1.4' so the music+SFX silence lands before the reversal. But duck_music.py picks the silence-beat location itself — 'the scene whose VO starts nearest 50% of the runtime' (line 75) — and IGNORES the writer's gap= for LOCATION (gap only sizes the fade if it happens to coincide). On samurai the story reversal is the beheading of the mentor at t14 (337s, 44% of a 761s runtime), but because the LATER scenes are longer (dialogue lines + gap=0.7 holds at t24/t26 push the TIME-midpoint past the STORY-midpoint), duck picked t15 (369s, the rival's taunt right after) as nearest-50%, so the silence landed one scene AFTER the intended reversal (still dramatic — it leads into Kenji's 'you put a blade to your own teacher' taunt — but not where the writer aimed it, and the writer's gap=1.4 on t13 did nothing for the silence). This mismatch will recur on ANY episode whose second half is heavier (dialogue/gaps) than its first, which is most of them (the payoff beats cluster late). CHEAP FIX: let a scene dict carry an explicit silence flag (e.g. gap>=1.4 OR a `silence=True` field) that OVERRIDES duck's 50%-nearest auto-pick, so the writer's marked pre-reversal scene is authoritative; fall back to the 50%-nearest heuristic only when no scene is flagged. Pairs with the dramatic-gap system already in gen_voice_edge (gap=0.7/1.4). RECURRED AGAIN on startup_unicorn (07-20): writer set gap=1.4 on t18 (the scene immediately before the t19 down-round reversal line, 50% mark by SCENE INDEX), but duck_music's log shows 'silence beat 0.44s in the gap before t16' instead — two scenes early, landing on the emptyChair/VC-pressure beat rather than the liquidation-preference reversal it was aimed at. Now 3-for-3 confirmed episodes (samurai, startup_unicorn, [ocean was template-error not this]) where the writer's explicit gap=1.4 placement is silently ignored by the 50%-nearest heuristic. Bumping impact med->high: this is a systematic, not occasional, mismatch and the fix is cheap (an explicit override flag, already scoped above). RECURRED A 4TH TIME on zombie_apocalypse (07-21): writer set gap=1.4 on t17 (the quiet 'Mara stops eating' scene, IMMEDIATELY before the t18 bite-reveal reversal line), but duck_music's log again reports 'silence beat 0.45s in the gap before t16' — one scene early, landing in the gap before the barracksLife/exhaustion beat instead of before the reversal. 4-for-4 now; still not fixed because the fix requires editing duck_music.py, which is outside the writer's allowed touch-set (content.py/episode_meta.json/scenes.tsx) for a routine content run — this needs a dedicated engineering pass, not another content-run workaround. COUNTER-EXAMPLE on venture_capitalist (07-24): the writer's gap=1.4 on t16 (the quiet 'phone doesn't buzz' scene, immediately before the t17 fraud-reveal reversal) landed CORRECTLY this time — duck_music.py's own log read 'silence beat 1.30s in the gap before t17', exactly where intended. First correct placement in 5 tracked episodes. Plausible reason, worth testing as a hypothesis rather than treating as confirmed: this script had only ONE other dramatic gap (gap=0.7 at the cold open t01, plus the mirrored gap=0.7 at the very last scene t33) and no dialogue-heavy back half, so nothing in the SECOND half of the runtime was heavier/longer than the first half — unlike the 4 prior mismatched episodes, which all had extra gap=0.7/1.4 holds or dialogue clustering AFTER their intended silence point, pulling the runtime-nearest-50% heuristic later than the scene-index midpoint. If this holds up across more episodes, the cheap mitigation until duck_music.py gets the real override-flag fix: keep dramatic gap=0.7/1.4 holds and dialogue scenes roughly BALANCED between the two halves of the script, not concentrated in the second half, so the writer's intended silence-beat scene stays close to the runtime midpoint the heuristic actually picks. Strengthens the case for the balanced-placement mitigation as a real, repeatable content-run workaround pending the actual override-flag fix in duck_music.py. Reserve figBehind for props with a real opening/frame the figure sits inside (life raft, chariot, cell bars) where the prop's shapes DON'T fully cover the figure's silhouette. CHEAP CHECKLIST for future vehicle/large-object props: sketch the prop's local bounding box, translate it to screen coords, and check whether the figure's default x/y falls inside it before deciding figBehind vs default order.

self_made_billionaire (07-27), FINAL REVIEWER catch (low severity): tried to differentiate two identical background-mourner extras (both `A.stand`, `pal: DIM`, `face: false`, front view) by giving the second one `view: 'profile'` plus a `headTilt` override, expecting it to read as a distinct turned/glancing figure per the narration ('a woman in a black coat glances back'). It rendered visually identical to the first -- in src/figure.tsx's StickFigure, `view`/`front` only changes which side ('near' vs 'far') the limb-mirroring uses (`ffar = front ? -facing : facing`); the <Face> component is called with `profile={false}` UNCONDITIONALLY, so the face itself never turns or changes shape based on `view`. LESSON: `view: 'profile'` alone is not a usable tool for visually distinguishing two otherwise-identical background figures in this rig -- it's a subtle limb-offset difference, not a silhouette change. To make a background figure read as distinct (a different person, a turned head, a glance), use `face: true` with a directional `expr` (e.g. FACES.conflicted has look:-0.45, 'uneasy, looking away') instead -- a visible eye/brow/mouth reads as a real differentiator at thumbnail-adjacent crowd scale where a blank oval does not.
